Chapter 6: Finding Comfort in Suffering and Loss
There are times in life when pain just seems to settle in, doesn’t it? Sometimes it shows up out of nowhere, and other times, it slowly takes root—leaving you feeling hollow, like nothing in your world fits the way it used to. When loss comes—whether suddenly or over time—it can be hard to even find the words to pray. Maybe you've felt that way: you know you need help, but prayer feels impossible. The words might not come at all, or if they do, they sound raw... angry, confused, maybe even desperate.
I want to share a story that might sound familiar. There was a woman, grieving the loss of her partner. She used to pray with ease, but now, the familiar words just felt empty. Most mornings, she couldn’t find much to say. So, she’d simply sit in her favorite chair, hands open in her lap. Sometimes, she’d whisper just one word—“Help.” Over time, something changed. She realized that just showing up—being present in her brokenness—became a kind of prayer. She began to sense a quiet presence with her. It didn’t take her pain away, but she wasn’t alone in it anymore.
Then there’s the father who suddenly lost his job. The hurt wasn’t just about the bills—it struck right at his sense of purpose and identity. In prayer, he let it all out: the anger, the confusion, sometimes even tears. Other times, he had nothing but silence. He found himself drawn to the Psalms—those ancient voices crying out in their own suffering. And it clicked for him: God isn’t far off from pain. He’s right there in the middle of it, listening, not judging. Most of us, when we suffer, want to move through it as quickly as possible. We look for answers or distractions—anything to ease the ache. But honest, daily prayer offers a different path. It encourages us to bring our pain into the open, to name it, and to trust that we’re not alone in it. The comfort that comes isn’t always big or dramatic. It’s more like someone reaching out and putting a hand on your shoulder. A quiet assurance that—even in the darkest times—hope is still there. With time, people who pray through their suffering often notice something shifting. The pain doesn’t feel quite so isolating. They spot small signs of comfort—a text from a friend, a beautiful sunrise, or a verse that speaks directly to their heart. These moments don’t erase the loss, but they do bring glimpses of healing. The journey through suffering is never easy. But daily prayer becomes a companion—a way to keep moving forward, just one day at a time.
